domain: electricity distribution operations / substation-day peak-stress exceedance prediction (retrospective)

jurisdiction.publisher: City of Cape Town (Energy Directorate via the Corporate GIS Open Data Portal, odp-cctegis.opendata.arcgis.com) - metropolitan municipality in South Africa

prediction_question: For each City of Cape Town switching substation, at 06:00 SAST on day D, predict whether that substation's evening peak apparent-power load (maximum half-hourly MVA reading over 16:00-22:00 SAST on day D) will exceed the trailing-90-evening 95th percentile of its own evening peaks (evenings ending strictly before the instant).
prediction_time: 06:00 Africa/Johannesburg (SAST, UTC+2) on day D, within the artifact's history. Features are the substation's half-hourly MVA readings with timestamps <= the instant (including day D's 00:00-06:00 readings), trailing aggregates computed only from readings <= the instant, plus calendar fields and substation identity. The evening target window 16:00-22:00 SAST lies entirely after the instant. RETROSPECTIVE USE: the publisher released the entire 2022-01-01..2024-12-31 window as one closed table (item created 2026-02-28, last modified 2026-03-02, hasStaticData), so this is a retrospective_research task per docs/PREDICTION-CONTRACT.md: no historical-operational-availability claim is made, label timing is unverified at any historical instant outside the artifact's own timestamp order.
target_definition: Binary: evening-peak exceedance. Label = (max half-hourly MVA over 16:00-22:00 SAST on day D for substation S) > (95th percentile of the same substation's evening peaks over the trailing 90 evenings ending strictly before the instant, minimum 30 prior evenings for eligibility). Label source columns: the target day's 16:00-22:00 MVA readings, plus the same substation's prior evening peaks; these are sealed (private label matrix) and never shipped in any solver-visible feature frame. The baseline operand (trailing p95) is computed from feature-side readings <= the instant and may ship as a numeric feature; the target evening readings cannot.

measurements.panel_shape_measured: 52,608 rows = 48 half-hours x 1,096 days, 2022-01-01 00:00 .. 2024-12-31 23:30 SAST, gapless (0 days with !=48 half-hours). 45 fields: Timestamp + 43 substation columns (33kV/66kV/132kV switching stations) + ObjectId. 41 double-typed substation columns have 52,608/52,608 non-null values (ZERO nulls); Triangle_132kV (string-typed) contains no values at all; Morgen_Gronde_132kV (string-typed) carries numeric readings stored as strings (schema artifact: parse at construction or exclude; measured on fetch). 42 stations carry data in total (41 double + Morgen Gronde parsed), and all 41 double-typed stations are used for the measured label counts.
measurements.target_labels_measured: Evening-peak p95-exceedance labels (trailing 90 evenings, min 30 prior evenings, evening window 16:00-22:00 SAST): 2022 positives 1,539/13,735 (11.20%); 2023 positives 1,256/14,965 (8.39%); 2024 positives 1,382/15,006 (9.21%). Total 4,177/43,706. Both classes present in every year. Commands in notes.md (probe_fullscan.py, probe_cluster.py).
measurements.clustering_measured: Positives cluster by day (city-wide weather / load-shedding regime): distinct exceedance days 2022: 227, 2023: 246, 2024: 247 (out of 365/365/366 label-bearing days), with all 41 stations carrying at least one positive in every year. The distinct-day counts are the clustered/independent-observation evidence for split capacity.
measurements.seasonality_fixture: Known-event fixture (verified measured): Cape Town winter evening-peaking. Monthly mean evening peak over all stations: 2024-07 61.9 MVA vs 2024-12 44.1 MVA; same May-August rise in 2022 (2022-08 60.3 vs 2022-12 48.0) and 2023 (2023-07 60.6 vs 2023-12 45.9). Per-station winter(May-Aug)/summer(Nov-Feb) mean evening-peak ratios: Grassy Park 66kV 1.25, Atlantis Industrial 132kV 1.22, Foreshore 132kV (CBD) 0.98 - winter-peaking residential/industrial substations and a flat CBD profile, exactly as expected for Cape Town's winter-heating, summer-cooling-mild coastal climate.
measurements.dated_worked_example: Grassy Park 66kV, Africa/Johannesburg (SAST): day D = 2024-07-15 (Monday, mid-winter). Feature event window = half-hourly readings 2022-01-01 00:00 .. 2024-07-15 06:00 for this substation (trailing aggregates computed within it); prediction instant = 2024-07-15 06:00 SAST; eligibility = >= 30 prior evenings (met: 90 evenings 2024-04-16..2024-07-14 used); target window = 2024-07-15 16:00-22:00 SAST (entirely after the instant); measured label = evening peak 150.38 MVA > trailing-90-evening p95 146.82 MVA -> POSITIVE. Every target-window timestamp is later than the instant; no target-window reading can be a feature.
measurements.extraction_cost_measured: 53 HTTP GETs (1,000 rows/page, orderByFields=ObjectId, outFields all), 70,086,470 bytes JSON, 54.1 s wall clock on the coordinator (4 vCPU / 1.9 GiB class), measured 2026-11-01. No raw copy retained: the fetch streams to per-station-day aggregates only (probe_fullscan.py); reduced aggregates ~9 MB. Advancement-side construction must re-fetch on a worker and pin sha256.
measurements.publisher_caveat: Item description (quoted): 'Users should note that readings are indicative of the measured Mega Volt-Ampere readings which have not been corrected for temporary load shifts due to operational requirements or load fluctuations due to load shedding.' The label therefore measures demand-as-dispatched, not underlying demand; this is documented meaning (usable), recorded as a limitation, and must appear in the dataset README.
measurements.cross_check_publisher_summary: The publisher ships no summary product for this table (raw readings only; the ODP page carries only the description quoted above). The internal consistency check is the arithmetic identity rows = 48 x 1,096 and the gapless daily grid, both measured. No publisher aggregate exists to contradict.
measurements.provenance_mix_measured: Single provenance stream: one reading per substation per half-hour from the City's SCADA/telemetry export; no sentinel/non-sentinel or multi-stream mixture. Two columns are string-typed (one empty, one numeric-as-text) - a schema artifact, not a separate population.
measurements.novelty_scope_limitations: Web search (arXiv, HF, GitHub, Fraunhofer survey) 2026-11-01; queries recorded by scripts/check-novelty.py. The Fraunhofer 25-dataset public load-forecasting survey lists system/zone/substation datasets from EU/US/AU operators only; no African substation series surfaced. Hugging Face/Zenodo catalogue searches for this source's title returned no ML-ready formulation of this task.

split_strategy: Temporal splits on station-days: train = 2022 (13,735 label-bearing station-days, 1,539 positives), eval = 2023 (14,965, 1,256), holdout = 2024 (15,006, 1,382). Disjoint years, both classes in every window, positives clustered on 227/246/247 distinct days per year. First ~30-90 evenings per station are burn-in (eligibility) and drop out of the labelled set. The evening-window 16:00-22:00 and the 06:00 instant are fixed for all splits; the sealed evening readings of any scored day never enter any shipped feature frame.
review: All five discovery contracts are supported with measured evidence: class A licence from the publisher's own instruments; a within-artifact 06:00 SAST instant with a fully-post-instant evening target window and publisher-documented feature meaning (with the load-shift caveat recorded as a limitation); a label derivable from the same gapless table with sealable label-source columns; measured split capacity (train 2022 / eval 2023 / holdout 2024, 1,256-1,539 positives per year, clustered on 227-247 distinct days); and a differentiated novelty position (regression forecasting benchmarks exist on EU/US/AU substation data; none is African, none is a within-day exceedance classification with a sealed label contract). Honest labelling: retrospective_research - the closed 2022-2024 window was published as one table in 2026, so no historical-operational-availability claim is made and label timing is unverified outside the artifact's own timestamp order.
next_action: Advancement owns construction on a worker: re-fetch all 52,608 rows and pin sha256; build station-day rows with features <= 06:00 instant and a sealed evening label matrix; splits 2022/2023/2024; full-artifact qualification + exact-byte acceptance BEFORE any quoted number (the abs-visitor-arrivals cross-row defect applies here by shape: a later same-station row's feature window contains this row's evening label operand - enforce isolated_rows prediction and keep evening readings out of all solver-visible frames, then run the reverse-history probes per docs/PREDICTION-CONTRACT.md); reference baselines (base-rate, prior-evening persistence, calendar/climatology) before model comparison. Open non-blocking question: whether the publisher extends the series beyond 2024 (item static since 2026-03).
uncertainty: Publisher extension of the series beyond 2024 is unknown (sibling prepaid item IS extended monthly; this item hasStaticData since 2026-03). Does not block v1 on the closed window.

novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
